Over 1,200 master craftsmen were employed to ensure every inch of the structure reflects traditional Moroccan artisanal excellence. The design features a hidden underground tunnel system to ensure staff can provide seamless service to the private three-story riads. From silver-inlaid furniture to hand-carved plaster, the building represents the absolute peak of 21st-century palatial luxury and design. It acts as a living showcase of the best Moroccan architectural techniques preserved and perfected for future generations.
Marrakech.address: Rue Abou Abbas El Sebti, Medina, Marrakech 40000, Morocco

Marrakech.name: Saadian Tombs
Marrakech.description: This royal necropolis dates back to the late 16th century and serves as the final resting place for the Saadian dynasty. The complex is world-renowned for its Chamber of Twelve Columns, which features majestic Carrara marble and an exquisite cedarwood dome. For centuries, the tombs were hidden behind high walls and remained forgotten until their rediscovery via aerial photography in 1917. The site is divided into two main mausoleums set within a tranquil garden filled with over one hundred mosaic-covered graves. It stands today as a breathtaking testament to the golden age of Islamic art and Moroccan craftsmanship during the reign of Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur.
Marrakech.address: 400 Rue de La Kasbah, Medina, Marrakech 40000, Morocco

Marrakech.name: Dar Si Said Museum
Marrakech.description: Dar Si Said is a magnificent 19th-century palatial residence that now serves as the National Museum of Weaving and Carpets. Built by the brother of the Grand Vizier who commissioned Bahia Palace, it showcases a similarly opulent display of Moroccan domestic architecture. The building is unique in the Medina for being constructed over multiple levels and featuring a spectacular upper-floor reception hall. Its central riad garden contains a beautifully painted wooden pavilion that is considered a masterpiece of the era's decorative arts. Today, it preserves an extensive collection of tribal jewelry, traditional weapons, and world-class textiles from across the Moroccan kingdom.
Marrakech.address: 8 Rue de la Bahia, Riad Zitoun Jdid, Marrakech 40000, Morocco

Lima.name: Torre Banco de la Nación
Lima.description: Standing as the tallest building in Peru, this skyscraper is a definitive landmark of Lima's modern financial district. It features a distinctive 'folded' glass facade designed to reflect the dynamic sky and the surrounding San Borja urban landscape. The tower was engineered specifically to withstand the region's high seismic activity through advanced structural damping. It serves as the primary headquarters for the nation's bank and the financial heartbeat of the country. This contemporary structure represents Peru's rapid economic growth and architectural modernization over the last decade.
Lima.address: Avenida Javier Prado Este 2465, San Borja, Lima 15037, Peru

Lima.name: Cathedral of Lima
Lima.description: This historic Roman Catholic cathedral is the centerpiece of Lima's UNESCO-listed Plaza Mayor. The structure has been meticulously rebuilt multiple times following major earthquakes throughout the centuries. These successive reconstructions have resulted in a unique architectural blend of Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque styles. Its exterior is famous for its massive carved wooden balconies and the warm hue of its sand-colored stone. Inside, the cathedral houses a museum and the tomb of the city's founder, Francisco Pizarro.
Lima.address: Jirón Carabaya s/n, Plaza de Armas, Cercado de Lima, Lima 15001, Peru

Lima.name: iSpace Jockey Plaza (Apple Premium)
Lima.description: Located within the prestigious Jockey Plaza shopping center, this flagship store represents the peak of retail technology in the city. The storefront features expansive open glass panels that create a seamless transition from the mall into the tech space. Inside, the minimalist wooden layout is modeled after the global 'Genius' design to provide a clean and organized aesthetic. It serves as a primary gathering hub for Lima's growing community of creative and tech professionals. The facility offers specialized support and training for the latest hardware and software ecosystems.
Lima.address: Avenida Javier Prado Este 4200, Santiago de Surco, Lima 15023, Peru

Lima.name: Convent of San Francisco
Lima.description: This monastery is a world-renowned example of Spanish Baroque architecture and a major cultural site in Peru. It is instantly recognizable by its vibrant yellow facade and the flock of pigeons that inhabit its expansive front courtyard. Beneath the church lie the famous subterranean catacombs which house the remains of over 25,000 people. The convent's library is considered one of the most beautiful in the world, containing thousands of ancient religious texts. Visitors can explore the intricate tile work and peaceful cloisters that offer a glimpse into colonial monastic life.
Lima.address: Jirón Lampa s/n, Cercado de Lima, Lima 15001, Peru

Lima.name: UTEC Campus
Lima.description: As the winner of the RIBA International Prize, this building is often described as a 'modern-day Machu Picchu.' The vertical concrete campus is designed with a series of open-air terraces that cascade down toward the Pacific Ocean. Its brutalist aesthetic purposely interacts with the coastal breeze to provide natural ventilation for the students. The structural engineering of the campus is a masterpiece of sustainable design and social integration. It serves as an innovation hub where the architecture itself encourages collaboration across different engineering disciplines.
Lima.address: Jirón Medrano Silva 165, Barranco, Lima 15063, Peru

Lima.name: Government Palace
Lima.description: Commonly known as the 'House of Pizarro,' this palace serves as the official residence and office of the President of Peru. It occupies a historically significant site where the original city foundation was established in 1535. The current Neo-Baroque structure features grand halls and ornate decorations that reflect French Neoclassical influences. A major tourist attraction is the daily changing of the guard ceremony held in the main courtyard. This building stands as a powerful symbol of the Peruvian executive branch and the country's political history.
Lima.address: Jirón de la Unión s/n, Plaza de Armas, Cercado de Lima, Lima 15001, Peru

Melbourne.name: Eureka Tower
Melbourne.description: This 91-story residential skyscraper is a prominent fixture of the Melbourne skyline named after the historic Eureka Stockade. The top ten floors are plated in 24-karat gold to symbolize the wealth generated during the 1850s Victorian gold rush. A distinct red stripe on the facade represents the blood spilled during the worker rebellion of 1854. Visitors can experience 'The Edge,' a glass cube that slides out from the building to suspend guests 285 meters above the ground. It remains one of the tallest residential buildings in the world and offers panoramic views of the entire city.
Melbourne.address: 7 Riverside Quay, Southbank, Melbourne VIC 3006, Australia

Melbourne.name: Flinders Street Station
Melbourne.description: As the busiest railway station in the Southern Hemisphere, this building serves as the heart of Melbourne's transport network. Its iconic French Renaissance design is instantly recognizable by its yellow facade and massive copper dome. The row of clocks at the main entrance remains the city's most popular meeting spot for locals and tourists alike. Completed in 1909, the station was once the busiest passenger station in the entire world. It continues to stand as a cultural landmark that bridges the gap between the historic city center and the Yarra River.
Melbourne.address: Flinders Street & Swanston Street, Melbourne VIC 3000, Australia

Melbourne.name: Apple Chadstone
Melbourne.description: This retail flagship is one of Apple's global architectural showcases designed to blend commerce with community. It features a massive, curved glass facade that spans the height of the storefront to invite natural light. The interior boasts a high-vaulted ceiling that integrates seamlessly with the luxury aesthetic of the surrounding shopping center. Central to the design is a dedicated 'Today at Apple' forum where visitors can engage in creative workshops. This location emphasizes the 'Town Square' concept by using bronze and stone materials to create an open, inviting environment.

Melbourne.name: Royal Exhibition Building
Melbourne.description: This historic landmark was the first building in Australia to be awarded UNESCO World Heritage status. Built for the 1880 International Exhibition, its massive dome was famously inspired by the Duomo in Florence. The structure remains a masterpiece of Victorian architecture, featuring intricate murals and expansive galleries. It has hosted significant historical events, including the opening of the first Parliament of Australia in 1901. Today, it continues to function as an active exhibition hall while being preserved as a symbol of the city's colonial era.
Melbourne.address: 9 Nicholson Street, Carlton, Melbourne VIC 3053, Australia

Melbourne.name: Federation Square
Melbourne.description: This bold, deconstructivist cultural hub is widely known for its unique and complex 'fractal' facade system. The various buildings are covered in a geometric zinc and sandstone grid that creates a striking visual texture. Since its opening in 2002, it has become one of the most polarizing and iconic public spaces in Australia. The square serves as a central gathering point for major public events, broadcasts, and artistic performances. It successfully connects the historic central business district with the modern developments along the Yarra River.
Melbourne.address: Swanston Street & Flinders Street, Melbourne VIC 3000, Australia

Melbourne.name: The Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia
Melbourne.description: This institution is the first major public gallery in the world dedicated exclusively to the exhibition of Australian art. The architecture is a seamless continuation of the Federation Square fractal style, utilizing sharp angles and raw materials. Inside, the space features complex glass 'shards' and vast atriums that allow light to filter through multiple levels. It houses an extensive collection of Indigenous and non-Indigenous artworks that span the history of the nation. The building's layout encourages visitors to navigate a non-linear path through the diverse stories of Australian culture.
